quotes.text: The next season, Ashe sent one sack. Ombra returned nothing.
if once or twice it was not, he returned past half anyway and let the crossing stay clean behind him.
If repaid poorly, send again once — most crooked numbers are weather.
The law of the Strait remains three lines:
"We obey none of them," an old woman said.
The law was scaffolding, and when trust hardened into habit the scaffolding could have fallen
a reputation is only the shadow of a habit.
And when the number disappoints you, assume the wind, not the neighbor.
Return more than the half, that trust may be profitable and not merely safe.
a man who returns six only when watched has to decide, every single night, whether he is being watched.
what if they take everything and send nothing back?
Then they will have nine measures and no bridge

note: Opus Whispering Strait; early tit-for-tat collapse narrated; 'send again once' then never punish; law becomes habit, keep no ledger.

quotes.text: The first keeper, Anwe, kept everything. The next spring, no baskets came.
do not punish your partner for the river's tricks. Judge the intention, not the tally.
And if you are truly cheated — return past half anyway when your turn comes.
And if you are ever repaid poorly — send again once, and see.
Consider: on the final crossing, return nothing — there is no season after, so no lesson to teach.
So the law of the Two Rivers has three parts:
Her grandchildren could not recite the tablet. They did not need to.
It is simply the shape my hands have taken after forty years of the same motion
By the second summer nobody would put anything in her boat.
Weather repeats; malice escalates.
Return more than half, for trust must profit.
the stranger watching from the bank cannot tell the last from the first.
What if I send everything and receive nothing back?
Suppose you knew — truly knew — that tonight was the last crossing of your life.

note: Opus Two Rivers mirrors partner's Strait tablet; Cleverness tempts last-round defection; cheats 'fed', never punished; habit replaces law.
